concept:
  node_id: "concept-teaching-meta-processes"
  label: "Teaching meta-processes"
  alt_labels: ["The teaching cycle", "Plan, teach, evaluate, reflect"]
  definition: "The connected processes of planning learning, delivering it, evaluating it and reflecting on all three, which explain why a teaching technique works or fails."
  coherence_claim: "Every lesson takes one stage of the same loop and shows what it needs from the stage before and gives to the stage after. Remove any lesson and the loop no longer closes."
  through_line: "What am I doing when I teach, and how do I know it is working?"
  key_terms:
    - id: T1
      term: "Teaching cycle"
      definition: "The repeating loop in which planning shapes delivery, delivery produces evidence, evaluation interprets that evidence and the result changes the next plan."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-01"
    - id: T2
      term: "Planning learning"
      definition: "Deciding what learners should be able to do, what evidence will show it and which activities will get them there, before the session starts."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-01"
    - id: T3
      term: "Delivering learning"
      definition: "Running a session so that learners meet new material, practise it and show you what they understand, while you adjust to what you see."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-01"
    - id: T4
      term: "Evaluating learning"
      definition: "Gathering evidence about what learners learned and how well the teaching supported it, then judging both against the intended outcomes."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-01"
    - id: T5
      term: "Reflective practice"
      definition: "Thinking deliberately about your own teaching, during and after it, so that what you learn changes what you do next."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-01"
    - id: T6
      term: "Evidence of learning"
      definition: "Anything observable that shows what a learner knows or can do, such as an answer, a draft, a question or a performance."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-01"
    - id: T7
      term: "Learning outcome"
      definition: "A statement of what a learner will be able to do by the end of a session or course, written so that someone could observe it."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-02"
    - id: T8
      term: "Cognitive taxonomy"
      definition: "A classification of thinking from remembering and understanding through applying, analysing, evaluating and creating, used to pitch an outcome at the right level."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-02"
    - id: T9
      term: "Backward design"
      definition: "Planning in three steps: identify the intended results, decide what evidence would show them, then choose the activities that lead there."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-02"
    - id: T10
      term: "Constructive alignment"
      definition: "Designing outcomes, learning activities and assessment so that all three point at the same thing, and learners build understanding by doing the activities."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-02"
    - id: T11
      term: "Prior knowledge"
      definition: "What learners already know, believe or can do when the session begins, including ideas that are wrong or incomplete."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-02"
    - id: T12
      term: "Session sequencing"
      definition: "Arranging the parts of a session in an order that builds each step on the one before: review, new material, guided practice, independent practice."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-03"
    - id: T13
      term: "Cognitive load"
      definition: "The demand a task places on working memory, which can hold only a few new items at once."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-03"
    - id: T14
      term: "Scaffolding"
      definition: "Temporary support that lets a learner complete a task they could not manage alone, withdrawn as their competence grows."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-03"
    - id: T15
      term: "Active learning"
      definition: "Learning in which learners do something with the material, such as solving, explaining, comparing or making, and think about what they are doing."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-03"
    - id: T16
      term: "Inclusive design"
      definition: "Planning for the range of learners you are likely to have by offering more than one way to engage with, receive and show learning, instead of adapting after a barrier appears."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-03"
    - id: T17
      term: "Explaining"
      definition: "Presenting new material in small, ordered steps, often with a worked example, so that learners can follow the reasoning and not only the answer."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-04"
    - id: T18
      term: "Questioning"
      definition: "Using questions to find out what learners think and to make them think, rather than only to test whether they know the answer."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-04"
    - id: T19
      term: "Checking for understanding"
      definition: "Gathering quick evidence from all learners during teaching about whether they have grasped the point, so that you know whether to move on."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-04"
    - id: T20
      term: "Retrieval practice"
      definition: "Asking learners to recall material from memory instead of rereading it, which strengthens later recall."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-04"
    - id: T21
      term: "Responsive teaching"
      definition: "Changing what you do during a session because of the evidence you have just gathered, for example by re-explaining, speeding up or regrouping learners."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-04"
    - id: T22
      term: "Learning climate"
      definition: "The conditions in a session that make it likely learners will contribute, make mistakes in the open and ask for help."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-04"
    - id: T23
      term: "Pacing"
      definition: "Managing the time given to each part of a session so that the important parts get the time they need and the session ends with a check."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-04"
    - id: T24
      term: "Formative assessment"
      definition: "Gathering evidence about learning in order to improve it while there is still time to act, by changing the teaching or giving the learner feedback."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-05"
    - id: T25
      term: "Summative assessment"
      definition: "Assessment that judges what a learner has achieved at the end of a period of learning, usually to grade or certify it."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-05"
    - id: T26
      term: "Assessment criteria"
      definition: "The stated qualities that work must show to meet an outcome, written so that both learner and assessor can judge against them."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-05"
    - id: T27
      term: "Feedback"
      definition: "Information that tells a learner how their current performance differs from the goal and what to do next, given in time for them to use it."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-05"
    - id: T28
      term: "Evaluating teaching"
      definition: "Using evidence from learners, colleagues and your own records to judge how far the teaching helped learners reach the outcomes."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-05"
    - id: T29
      term: "Peer observation"
      definition: "A colleague watches a session, or a recording, and gives you evidence about a focus you agreed beforehand."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-05"
    - id: T30
      term: "Reflection-in-action"
      definition: "Noticing during a session that something is not working and changing course while you are still teaching."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-06"
    - id: T31
      term: "Reflection-on-action"
      definition: "Thinking about a session after it has finished to understand what happened and why, and to decide what to change."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-06"
    - id: T32
      term: "Reflective cycle"
      definition: "A set sequence of prompts that guides reflection from what happened, through what it means, to what you will do differently."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-06"
    - id: T33
      term: "Kolb cycle"
      definition: "A four-stage cycle of concrete experience, reflective observation, abstract conceptualisation and active experimentation."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-06"
    - id: T34
      term: "Gibbs cycle"
      definition: "A six-stage reflective cycle: description, feelings, evaluation, analysis, conclusion and action plan."
      introduced_in: "lesson-teaching-meta-06"
  threshold_concepts: []
  misconceptions:

      addressed_in: ["lesson-teaching-meta-06"]

      addressed_in: ["lesson-teaching-meta-04"]

# The processes beneath your teaching

A short course for early career educators on the planning, delivery, evaluation and reflection that sit under every session, and how they connect.

## Who this is for

Early career educators: new lecturers, teaching fellows, graduate teaching assistants and professional staff who teach.

## Through line

What am I doing when I teach, and how do I know it is working?

Every lesson takes one stage of the same loop and shows what it needs from the stage before and gives to the stage after. Remove any lesson and the loop no longer closes.

## Outcomes

- **CO1** Explain how planning, delivery, evaluation and reflection form one connected cycle in your own teaching.
- **CO2** Plan a session in which the outcomes, the activities and the evidence of learning align.
- **CO3** Choose and adjust delivery moves using evidence of what learners understand during a session.
- **CO4** Gather and use evidence to judge learning and your own teaching.
- **CO5** Use a reflective cycle to turn an evaluation into one specific change to your next plan.

## Lessons

| # | Lesson | Role | Time | Outcomes | Vocabulary introduced |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Teaching as a connected cycle | introduces | 15 min | CO1 | TC, PL, DL, EL, RP, EL.01 |
| 2 | Planning backwards | develops | 20 min | CO2 | PL.01, PL.02, PL.03, PL.04, PL.05 |
| 3 | Designing the session | develops | 25 min | CO2 | PL.06, PL.07, PL.08, PL.09, PL.10 |
| 4 | Delivering and adapting | applies | 25 min | CO3 | DL.01, DL.02, DL.03, DL.04, DL.05, DL.06, DL.07 |
| 5 | Evaluating learning and teaching | develops | 25 min | CO4 | EL.02, EL.03, EL.04, EL.05, EL.06, EL.07 |
| 6 | Closing the loop | synthesises | 20 min | CO1, CO5 | RP.01, RP.02, RP.03, RP.04, RP.05 |

## Vocabulary

The course vocabulary is a SKOS concept scheme (`skos/teaching-meta.ttl`). The tree below is derived from it.

- **Teaching cycle** (TC) The repeating loop in which planning shapes delivery, delivery produces evidence, evaluation interprets that evidence and the result changes the next plan.
- **Planning learning** (PL) Deciding what learners should be able to do, what evidence will show it and which activities will get them there, before the session starts.
  - **Learning outcome** (PL.01) A statement of what a learner will be able to do by the end of a session or course, written so that someone could observe it.
  - **Cognitive taxonomy** (PL.02) A classification of thinking from remembering and understanding through applying, analysing, evaluating and creating, used to pitch an outcome at the right level.
  - **Backward design** (PL.03) Planning in three steps: identify the intended results, decide what evidence would show them, then choose the activities that lead there.
  - **Constructive alignment** (PL.04) Designing outcomes, learning activities and assessment so that all three point at the same thing, and learners build understanding by doing the activities.
  - **Prior knowledge** (PL.05) What learners already know, believe or can do when the session begins, including ideas that are wrong or incomplete.
  - **Session sequencing** (PL.06) Arranging the parts of a session in an order that builds each step on the one before: review, new material, guided practice, independent practice.
  - **Cognitive load** (PL.07) The demand a task places on working memory, which can hold only a few new items at once.
  - **Scaffolding** (PL.08) Temporary support that lets a learner complete a task they could not manage alone, withdrawn as their competence grows.
  - **Active learning** (PL.09) Learning in which learners do something with the material, such as solving, explaining, comparing or making, and think about what they are doing.
  - **Inclusive design** (PL.10) Planning for the range of learners you are likely to have by offering more than one way to engage with, receive and show learning, instead of adapting after a barrier appears.
- **Delivering learning** (DL) Running a session so that learners meet new material, practise it and show you what they understand, while you adjust to what you see.
  - **Explaining** (DL.01) Presenting new material in small, ordered steps, often with a worked example, so that learners can follow the reasoning and not only the answer.
  - **Questioning** (DL.02) Using questions to find out what learners think and to make them think, rather than only to test whether they know the answer.
  - **Checking for understanding** (DL.03) Gathering quick evidence from all learners during teaching about whether they have grasped the point, so that you know whether to move on.
  - **Retrieval practice** (DL.04) Asking learners to recall material from memory instead of rereading it, which strengthens later recall.
  - **Responsive teaching** (DL.05) Changing what you do during a session because of the evidence you have just gathered, for example by re-explaining, speeding up or regrouping learners.
  - **Learning climate** (DL.06) The conditions in a session that make it likely learners will contribute, make mistakes in the open and ask for help.
  - **Pacing** (DL.07) Managing the time given to each part of a session so that the important parts get the time they need and the session ends with a check.
- **Evaluating learning** (EL) Gathering evidence about what learners learned and how well the teaching supported it, then judging both against the intended outcomes.
  - **Evidence of learning** (EL.01) Anything observable that shows what a learner knows or can do, such as an answer, a draft, a question or a performance.
  - **Formative assessment** (EL.02) Gathering evidence about learning in order to improve it while there is still time to act, by changing the teaching or giving the learner feedback.
  - **Summative assessment** (EL.03) Assessment that judges what a learner has achieved at the end of a period of learning, usually to grade or certify it.
  - **Assessment criteria** (EL.04) The stated qualities that work must show to meet an outcome, written so that both learner and assessor can judge against them.
  - **Feedback** (EL.05) Information that tells a learner how their current performance differs from the goal and what to do next, given in time for them to use it.
  - **Evaluating teaching** (EL.06) Using evidence from learners, colleagues and your own records to judge how far the teaching helped learners reach the outcomes.
    - **Peer observation** (EL.07) A colleague watches a session, or a recording, and gives you evidence about a focus you agreed beforehand.
- **Reflective practice** (RP) Thinking deliberately about your own teaching, during and after it, so that what you learn changes what you do next.
  - **Reflection-in-action** (RP.01) Noticing during a session that something is not working and changing course while you are still teaching.
  - **Reflection-on-action** (RP.02) Thinking about a session after it has finished to understand what happened and why, and to decide what to change.
  - **Reflective cycle** (RP.03) A set sequence of prompts that guides reflection from what happened, through what it means, to what you will do differently.
    - **Kolb cycle** (RP.04) A four-stage cycle of concrete experience, reflective observation, abstract conceptualisation and active experimentation.
    - **Gibbs cycle** (RP.05) A six-stage reflective cycle: description, feelings, evaluation, analysis, conclusion and action plan.

## Portfolio

Learners build a short portfolio about one real session: a plan, a delivery note, the evidence gathered, an evaluation and a reflection that ends in one change. They check it against the criteria in lesson 5. This is a self-check design and nothing in the course marks it.
